AI / Signal Processing (ai/)¶

IMU signal preprocessing, feature extraction, spectrogram conversion, and the standalone model-training experiments (BiLSTM, GRU, window-based CNN/XGBoost). These modules are not part of the live GPS-only app — they support the separate IMU/ML work. Heavy dependencies (torch, xgboost, sklearn, scipy, matplotlib) are mocked at build time, so the docs render from the docstrings without those packages installed.

ai.features¶

Hand-crafted IMU feature extraction for the turn/hill window classifier.

Collapses a fixed (100, 9) window of preprocessed IMU samples ([gyro_xyz | accel_xyz | mag_xyz]) into a fixed-length vector of N_FEATURES statistics — per-axis mean/std/extremes, threshold-crossing fractions, a gyro-Z / accel-Y correlation, and energy terms. The width is fixed so it can feed a model with a constant input size.

AutoDNA.ai.features.N_FEATURES = 36¶

Length of the vector returned by extract_features().

AutoDNA.ai.features.extract_features(window)[source]¶

Compute the N_FEATURES-length feature vector for one IMU window.

Parameters:

window (ndarray) – (100, 9) float array, columns [gyro_xyz|accel_xyz|mag_xyz].

Returns:

(N_FEATURES,) float32 vector. Zero-variance inputs (e.g. a stationary vehicle) are guarded so the correlation / ratio terms never return NaN.

Return type:

ndarray

ai.raw_to_inputs¶

Created on Thu May 14 17:07:08 2026

@author: mihal

build_training_data.py¶

Batch pipeline that converts raw sensor recordings (.npz) into compressed training samples for the AutoDNA driving-event classifier.

For every recording found in PARSED_DIR that has a matching label file in LABELED_DIR, the pipeline:

  1. Loads and resamples multi-axis IMU data onto a common time grid.

  2. Pre-processes (low-pass filters) the signals.

  3. Selects STFT parameters suited to the recording length and sampling rate.

  4. Converts every sensor axis to an RGB spectrogram image.

  5. Computes per-window statistics (mean) for gyro Z, gyro Y, and accel X — these preserve signal sign and magnitude for downstream direction / tilt regression heads.

  6. Aligns the JSON event labels to the spectrogram time axis, producing a dense (T × 7) label matrix.

  7. Writes everything to a single compressed .npz file under input_data/.

Label column layout (axis 1 of the label matrix)¶

0 — is_turn binary flag: 1 if a turn event is active 1 — turn_dir binary flag: 1 = right, 0 = left (valid when col 0 = 1) 2 — turn_angle normalised angle in [0, 1] (clipped at MAX_ANGLE_TURN) 3 — is_hill binary flag: 1 if a hill event is active 4 — hill_dir binary flag: 1 = uphill, 0 = downhill (valid when col 3 = 1) 5 — hill_angle normalised angle in [0, 1] (clipped at MAX_ANGLE_HILL) 6 — is_straight binary flag: 1 if the road segment is straight

AutoDNA.ai.raw_to_inputs.compute_mean_per_window(gyro_z_signal, nperseg, noverlap)[source]¶

Compute the arithmetic mean of a signal within each STFT window.

The windowing scheme mirrors the one used by scipy.signal.stft() / the project’s spectrogram conversion so that the returned array is index-aligned with the spectrogram time axis.

Sign is deliberately not rectified: positive values indicate one physical direction and negative values the opposite, which is necessary for the model’s direction regression heads (e.g. left vs. right turn, uphill vs. downhill).

Note

Trailing samples that do not fill a complete window of length nperseg are silently discarded, consistent with scipy.signal.stft default behaviour (boundary=None).

Parameters:

  • gyro_z_signal (numpy.ndarray) – 1-D array of pre-processed sensor samples. Although the parameter is named gyro_z_signal for historical reasons, the function is axis-agnostic and can be used with any 1-D signal (gyro Y, accel X, etc.).

  • nperseg (int) – STFT window length in samples.

  • noverlap (int) – Number of overlapping samples between consecutive windows. The hop size is nperseg - noverlap.

Returns:

Float32 array of per-window means, shape (T,) where T is the number of complete windows.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

AutoDNA.ai.raw_to_inputs.compute_pitch_angle_signal(accel_x, accel_z)[source]¶

Compute pitch angle with mounting offset removed. Uses median of first 5 seconds as baseline (assumes car starts on flat road).

AutoDNA.ai.raw_to_inputs.get_log_number(npz_path)[source]¶

Extract the numeric index from a log filename e.g. LOG005 -> 5.

AutoDNA.ai.raw_to_inputs.labels_to_timeseries(labels, times)[source]¶

Convert a list of labelled event segments into a dense per-column label matrix aligned to the spectrogram time axis.

Each segment in labels contributes to every spectrogram column whose centre time falls within [t_start, t_end] (inclusive). Overlapping segments are supported: later segments in the list simply overwrite earlier ones for the overlapping columns.

Parameters:

  • labels (list[dict]) –

    List of segment dicts. Recognised keys per segment:

    • t_start (float, required) — segment start time in seconds.

    • t_end (float, required) — segment end time in seconds.

    • straight (any truthy value, optional) — marks a straight road section; sets column 6 to 1.0.

    • turn (dict, optional) — turn event with sub-keys:

      • dir (str) — 'right' or 'left'.

      • angleDeg (float) — unsigned turn angle in degrees.

    • hill (dict, optional) — hill event with sub-keys:

      • dir (str) — 'up' or 'down'.

      • angleDeg (float) — unsigned hill angle in degrees.

  • times (numpy.ndarray) – 1-D array of STFT column centre times (seconds), shape (T,).

Returns:

Float32 label matrix of shape (T, 7). See module docstring for column definitions.

Return type:

numpy.ndarray

AutoDNA.ai.raw_to_inputs.main()[source]¶

Run axis-correction and sensor sanity plots, then export training samples.

The verification plots run first; the export loop over LOG_FILES (below) resamples, preprocesses, and writes one .npz training sample per recording via save_training_sample().

AutoDNA.ai.raw_to_inputs.plot_pitch_vs_labels(parsed_dir, label_dir, log_num)[source]¶

Plot computed pitch angle alongside hill labels to verify correctness. Uphill regions should show positive pitch, downhill negative.

AutoDNA.ai.raw_to_inputs.sanity_check_sensors(parsed_dir, log_num)[source]¶

Print statistics for a file to verify sensor readings make sense. At rest: accel_z ≈ ±1000mg, accel_x/y ≈ 0, gyro_x/y/z ≈ 0

AutoDNA.ai.raw_to_inputs.save_training_sample(npz_path, converted, labels, processed, nperseg, noverlap, output_dir)[source]¶

Save one recording’s spectrogram, per-window statistics, and labels as a single compressed .npz file.

The file written to output_dir contains the following arrays:

  • <sensor>_rgb — uint8 RGB spectrogram image for each sensor axis, shape (H, W, 3).

  • <sensor>_times — float32 centre times (s) of each STFT column, shape (T,).

  • <sensor>_freqs — float32 frequency bin centres (Hz), shape (F,).

  • gyro_z_mean_per_window — float32 raw gyro-Z mean per window, shape (T,). Sign is preserved so the model can infer turn direction.

  • gyro_y_mean_per_window — float32 raw gyro-Y mean per window, shape (T,). Sign preserved for pitch direction.

  • accel_x_mean_per_window — float32 raw accel-X mean per window, shape (T,). Sign preserved for forward/backward acceleration.

  • labels — float32 dense label matrix, shape (T, 7). See module docstring for column definitions.

Parameters:

  • npz_path (str or pathlib.Path) – Path to the source recording .npz file. Used only to derive the output filename.

  • converted (dict[str, dict]) – Mapping returned by convert_all_sensors_to_spectrograms(). Keys are sensor names; values are dicts with keys 'rgb_image', 'times', and 'frequencies'.

  • labels (list[dict]) – List of label segment dicts loaded from the JSON label file. Each dict must contain at minimum 't_start' and 't_end' keys, plus optional 'straight', 'turn', and 'hill' sub-dicts.

  • processed (dict[str, dict[str, numpy.ndarray]]) – Pre-processed sensor data as returned by preprocess_sensor_data(). Expected structure: {'gyro': {'x', 'y', 'z'}, 'accel': {'x', 'y', 'z'}}.

  • nperseg (int) – STFT window length in samples (must match the value used to produce converted).

  • noverlap (int) – Number of samples of overlap between consecutive STFT windows (must match the value used to produce converted).

  • output_dir (str or pathlib.Path) – Directory where the .npz training file is written. Created automatically if it does not exist.

Returns:

Path of the newly written .npz file.

Return type:

pathlib.Path

AutoDNA.ai.raw_to_inputs.swap_axes_90_left_flip(sensors)[source]¶

Correct axis orientation for files where sensor points to left window. Sensor X points left, Y points backward — swap to standard (X=forward, Y=left).

standard_x = -sensor_y standard_y = sensor_x standard_z = sensor_z (unchanged)

AutoDNA.ai.raw_to_inputs.swap_axes_90_right_flip(sensors)[source]¶

Correct axis orientation for files where sensor points to right window. Sensor X points right, Y points forward — swap to standard (X=forward, Y=left).

standard_x = sensor_y standard_y = -sensor_x standard_z = sensor_z (unchanged)

BiLSTM experiments¶

ai.bilstm.bilstm¶

Created on Thu May 14 16:45:16 2026

@author: mihal

class AutoDNA.ai.bilstm.bilstm.BiLSTM(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: Module

Bidirectional LSTM network for per-timestep classification of driving maneuvers.

The network accepts a time series of sensor data and predicts 7 values for each timestep: turn presence and direction, hill presence and direction, their respective angles, and a straight driving indicator.

Architecture: BiLSTM -> Dropout -> Linear -> Sigmoid

Parameters:

input_size – Size of the input vector per timestep.

forward(x)[source]¶

Perform one forward pass through the network.

Parameters:

x – Input tensor of shape (batch, T, input_size).

Returns:

Output tensor of shape (batch, T, 7) with values in [0, 1]. Outputs are: - col 0: turn_present - col 1: turn_dir (0=left, 1=right) - col 2: turn_angle normalized to [0, 1] - col 3: hill_present - col 4: hill_dir (0=down, 1=up) - col 5: hill_angle normalized to [0, 1] - col 6: straight

class AutoDNA.ai.bilstm.bilstm.DriveDataset(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Bases: Dataset

PyTorch Dataset for loading training samples from .npz files.

Each sample is one drive sequence with all sensor data and labels for every timestep.

Parameters:

sample_files – List of paths to .npz training files.

Calculate pos_weight for each binary output from training data. Capped at max_weight to prevent extreme imbalance dominating loss.

AutoDNA.ai.bilstm.bilstm.evaluate_model(model, validation_files)[source]¶

Run detailed evaluation of the model on validation files.

Measures and prints: - Presence accuracy for turn, hill and straight. - Direction accuracy for turn and hill (only where events are present). - Mean absolute angle error for turn and hill in degrees.

Parameters:

  • model – Trained BiLSTM model in eval mode.

  • validation_files – List of paths to validation .npz files.

AutoDNA.ai.bilstm.bilstm.flatten_sensors(accel, gyro, mag)[source]¶

Combine RGB spectrograms from all three sensors into one time series.

Each sensor has shape (F, T, 3). The frequency and color dimensions are flattened into one vector and transposed to (T, F*3). All three sensors are concatenated along the time axis.

Parameters:

  • accel – Accelerometer RGB spectrogram of shape (F, T, 3).

  • gyro – Gyroscope RGB spectrogram of shape (F, T, 3).

  • mag – Magnetometer RGB spectrogram of shape (F, T, 3).

Returns:

Matrix of shape (T, F*9) where each row represents one timestep with all sensor values.

AutoDNA.ai.bilstm.bilstm.into_deterministic(pred)[source]¶

Convert raw model predictions into deterministic decisions.

Applies sigmoid to convert raw logits to probabilities, then thresholds binary outputs to 0 or 1. Angle outputs are converted from normalized values to degrees.

Parameters:

pred – Raw logit tensor of shape (batch, T, 7).

Returns:

Tensor of shape (batch, T, 7) with binary decisions and angles in degrees.

AutoDNA.ai.bilstm.bilstm.masked_loss(pred, target, pw)[source]¶

Multi-task loss computed over labelled timesteps only.

Sums pos-weighted BCE for turn/hill/straight presence and direction plus an L1 term on the two normalised angle outputs. Timesteps whose target row is all-zero (unlabelled) are masked out. pw maps head names to pos-weights.

GRU experiment¶

ai.gru.train¶

GRU sequence classifier experiment (per-drive maneuver classification).

Loads RGB-spectrogram .npz samples, flattens all three sensors into one time series per drive, and trains a GRU to predict a single class label for the whole sequence. Standalone research script — not used by the live app.

Window-based CNN / XGBoost¶

ai.window_based.build_dataset¶

Minimal Pipeline za pripravo training dataseta iz IMU .npz logov. Kanali (4): gyro_z, accel_x, accel_y, accel_z

Poenostavljen label assignment brez kompliciranih pragov.

AutoDNA.ai.window_based.build_dataset.main()[source]¶

Window every labelled recording and save the concatenated turn/hill .npy arrays.

AutoDNA.ai.window_based.build_dataset.make_windows(signal, t, labels, log_idx, window_size, stride, label_key)[source]¶

Slide a fixed window over signal and emit (X, Y, log_ids) arrays.

Each window is labelled by the dominant turn/hill class overlapping its time span; log_idx tags every window with its source recording (for GroupKFold).

Returns:

((X_turn, Y_turn, ids_turn), (X_hill, Y_hill, ids_hill)).

Odšteje začetno povprečje (mentor’s trick) za odstranitev statičnega biasa.

ai.window_based.train_cnn¶

Popravljen minimalni 1D CNN z GroupKFold CV, utežmi za balansiranje, Focal Loss funkcijo ter popravljeno časovno ločljivostjo za klančine.

class AutoDNA.ai.window_based.train_cnn.FocalLoss(alpha=None, gamma=2.0)[source]¶

Bases: Module

Multi-class focal loss with optional per-class alpha weighting.

Down-weights easy examples via the (1 - pt) ** gamma factor so rare classes (e.g. hills) contribute more to the gradient.

forward(inputs, targets)[source]¶

Return the mean focal loss for logits inputs against class targets.

class AutoDNA.ai.window_based.train_cnn.MinimalIMUDataset(X, Y, augment=False)[source]¶

Bases: Dataset

Windowed IMU dataset yielding (C, T) tensors for SimpleCNN.

With augment enabled, the accel X/Y axes are randomly rotated to make the turn/hill classifier invariant to sensor mounting yaw.

class AutoDNA.ai.window_based.train_cnn.SimpleCNN(n_channels=4, n_classes=3)[source]¶

Bases: Module

Compact 1-D CNN classifier for fixed-length IMU windows.

BatchNorm -> Conv -> ReLU -> MaxPool -> Conv -> ReLU -> AdaptiveAvgPool -> Linear, mapping n_channels input signals to n_classes logits.

forward(x)[source]¶

Run the conv stack on (N, C, T) input and return (N, n_classes) logits.
